candidates.title: Lionel Legacy SD38
candidates.excerpt: It’s been a while since Lionel has put out a diesel locomotive that makes you think, “Wow, they put a lot of detail into this.” I felt that way when unwrapping the Lionel SD38 recently. Trainworld loaned me a No. 2633341 SD38 free of charge for review. The SD38 was one of only 63 units built by EMD between May 1967 and October of 1971. The 16-cylinder prime mover put out about 2000 of non turbocharged horsepower. With six axles and 90,000 lbs. of tractive effort, the SD38 was primarily relegated to rail yards and occasional short distance hauling. The prototype SD38 No. 6925 was built in April 1970 for Penn Central. It was transferred to Conrail in April 1976. After the Conrail dissolved, it went to Norfolk Southern, and later the National Railway Equipment Company (NREX). It was scrapped in 2012. candidates.title: CMA CGM announces new RRI to US East Coast
candidates.excerpt: CMA CGM will apply a Rate Restoration Initiative (RRI) on cargo shipped from Türkiye and other Mediterranean-region ports to the US East Coast. The revised rates will take effect on 1 November 2026 and apply to tariff and service contract shipments. The second rate level covers the following origins: - East Mediterranean: Greece, Lebanon, Malta, Syria, Egypt and Cyprus - Black Sea: Bulgaria, Georgia, Romania and Ukraine - Adriatic: Albania, Croatia, Montenegro, Slovenia and Italy - North Africa: Algeria, Libya and Tunisia The increases apply to cargo moving to the US East Coast and inland destinations served through its ports. All cargo types are included except out-of-gauge shipments.

Global benchmarks also moved lower. Drewry’s World Container Index (WCI) and the Freightos Baltic Index (FBX) both declined 1%, while the Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) edged lower. The China Containerized Freight Index (CCFI), however, recorded a modest increase. Chinese freight indexes send mixed signals The SCFI declined 0.66% to 3,662.30 points from 3,686.62 in the previous reading. The broader CCFI moved in the opposite direction, increasing around 0.3% to 1,923.93 points from 1,917.68. No new Ningbo Containerized Freight Index (NCFI) reading was published due to China’s National Day holiday period. As a result, the previous NCFI reading has not been treated as a new weekly observation. candidates.title: Maersk revises terminal handling charges in Brazil
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will revise its Origin Handling Charge (OHC) and Destination Handling Charge (DHC) for containers moving to and from Brazil. The updated tariffs will take effect on 1 November 2026 and remain applicable until further notice. Maersk attributed the adjustment to higher port-related and operational costs. All rates are quoted in Brazilian reais per container. The same tariff levels apply to both origin and destination terminal handling services at each location.

candidates.title: InventHelp Inventors Develop New Accessory for Holding a Popcorn Container (BEC-464)
candidates.excerpt: PITTSBURGH, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- "We thought there should be a simple way to secure a container of popcorn to a cup holder," said one of two inventors, from Las Vegas, Nev., "so we invented the POP-CUP. Our design eliminates the need to hold the popcorn bag, and it could help prevent messy popcorn spills." The patent-pending invention provides a handsfree way to hold a bucket/bag of popcorn at a movie theater or other venue. In doing so, it eliminates the need to set the popcorn bag on the lap, floor, etc. As a result, it helps prevent popcorn spills and grease stains. The invention features a simple and practical design that is easy to attach and use so it is ideal for individuals of all ages at movie theaters, sporting events, carnivals, stadiums, etc. The original design was submitted to the National sales office of InventHelp. Another strong week for industrial rail freight
candidates.excerpt: U.S. weekly rail traffic totaled 537,397 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.85 compared with the same week a year ago, the Association of American Railroads (AAR) said. Traffic for the week ending September 26 totaled 235,787 carloads, up 3% compared with the same week in 2025, while intermodal volume of 301,610 containers and trailers was 6.3% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Seven of the 10 specific carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025.
